title: Thread a Tree Into a Right Chain
statement:
Rearrange a binary tree in place so that it becomes a single chain going down the right side. Every node's left must end up null, and following right pointers from the root must visit the nodes in pre-order: a node first, then its whole left subtree, then its whole right subtree.

Return nothing. The checker reads the tree from root after your function runs. Reuse the existing nodes; do not build new ones.

examples.why: Pre-order is 4, 2, 1, 3, 6, 5. The whole left subtree (2, 1, 3) comes before the right one (6, 5).
3 is the left child of 2. It must move to 2's right, and 2's left must be cleared.

hints: The final order is just pre-order. The easy version collects the nodes first and then relinks them. Can you avoid the list?
Look at one node with a left subtree. In pre-order, the last node of that left subtree comes right before the node's right child.
For each node with a left child: find the rightmost node of the left subtree, hang the current right subtree there, move the left subtree to the right and clear left. Then step right and repeat.

explain.intuition:
In pre-order, a node is followed by its left subtree, and the last node of that left subtree (its rightmost node) is followed by the node's right subtree. So you can splice locally: take the right subtree, hang it on the rightmost node of the left subtree, then move the left subtree into the right slot.

After one splice the current node has no left child, and its right child is the next node in pre-order. Step right and repeat. Every edge is walked a constant number of times in total, so this runs in O(n) with no extra memory, much like a Morris traversal.
steps: While cur is not null: if cur.left exists, find pre, the rightmost node of cur.left.
Set pre.right = cur.right, then cur.right = cur.left and cur.left = null.
pitfalls: Forgetting to set left = null. The chain looks right when you follow right, but the tree is not flattened.
Overwriting cur.right before saving it, which loses the whole right subtree.
Building new nodes. The task is to relink the existing ones, like moving DOM nodes instead of cloning them.

solutions.title: Collect pre-order, then relink
solutions.idea: Walk the tree in pre-order into an array with an explicit stack, then point each node's right at the next one and clear every left.

solutions.title: Splice the right subtree under the left one
solutions.idea: For each node with a left child, attach its right subtree to the rightmost node of the left subtree, then move the left subtree to the right.

followups: Do it recursively by visiting nodes in reverse pre-order (right, left, node) and keeping a pointer to the previously visited node.
Turn the tree into a sorted doubly linked list instead, using left as prev and right as next.
lcTitle: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
